chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-ʿUbaydi, from ʿAli ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be your sacrifice, I have no child, and I have estates which I inherited from my father, and some of them I acquired myself. I do not feel secure from unforeseen events. If I do not have a child and something happens to me, then what do you think, may I be your sacrifice: should I dedicate some of them as a waqf for the poor among my brothers and the weak, or should I sell them and give their price in charity to them during my lifetime? For I fear that the endowment may not be carried out after my death. If I endow them during my lifetime, may I eat from them during the days of my life, or not?

So he wrote, peace be upon him: I have understood your letter regarding your estates. It is not for you to eat from them, nor from the charity. If you eat from them, it will not be carried out, if you have heirs. So sell, and give some of their price in charity during your lifetime. If you give in charity, keep for yourself what sustains you, like what Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام did.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: charity given for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: the weak or socially vulnerable people
key_terms.الْوَقْفُ: the endowment of property for a pious or charitable purpose
key_terms.يَقُوتُكَ: what sustains or provides maintenance for you

ai.seo_question: Can a person endow property for the poor during his lifetime and still benefit from it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling on disposing of one's property through waqf or charity during one's lifetime when one fears death and has no child. The Imam عليه السلام rules that one should not continue benefiting from property designated as waqf or charity in a way that invalidates its execution, and advises selling some property and giving charity from its proceeds while retaining enough for personal maintenance.
